messages:
anna_support: FYI customer AcmeAI reporting a sudden flood of 504s from hosted inference around 09:12 UTC. P95 spiked from 120ms -> 3.2s. They included a sample request_id: req_0a1b2c3d and claim it repros under a small load test.

devon_infra: Can you paste the request_id and example curl? Also which model/route are they hitting?

anna_support: request_id=req_0a1b2c3d, org=acmeai, model=redwood-medium, route=/v1/generate. Example repro: `curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer <key>" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"model":"redwood-medium","input":"hello"}' -i` -> `HTTP/1.1 504 Gateway Timeout` after ~30s.

ingress-bot: Alert: ContinuousBatcher queue_depth=498/512, kv_miss_rate=62%, inflight_batches=89, average_batch_size=6.7 (09:11:58 UTC)

sam_oncall: Looks like the continuous-batcher backlog is pegged. High KV miss + high inflight_batches suggests cache warmup + pileup. Any recent rollout?

devon_infra: No model rollout in last 24h. I see a short burst from acmeai (traffic pattern: many concurrent small requests), causing batching to aggregate -> long queueing for tail requests. Our queue_depth soft-limit at 512 is hit, so tail waits until batch forms. That explains 504s when deadline is hit.

luis_sre: Also seeing retry amplification from their client: they resend on 502/504 immediately. Graph shows retry spikes at same times as backlog. That keeps persistence high.

anna_support: Customer says their client retries after 2s. We're basically amplifying the load. They're asking for immediate mitigation and a timeline.

sam_oncall: Immediate mitigations we can do now: 1) enable ingress shed for org=acmeai (drop excess at gateway) 2) lower per-worker concurrency from 8 -> 4 for the affected pool to reduce head-of-line blocking 3) temporarily enable model-fallback to redwood-small for acmeai route. Which is fastest?

devon_infra: I can flip 1) and 3) quickly. Shedding via routing rule and a model pin fallback are config changes (few minutes). Lowering concurrency requires a small rolling change but doable. Suggest order: shed -> fallback -> reduce concurrency.

ops-bot: Runbook check: `ingress.shed(org=acmeai) -> true` executed by devon_infra at 09:17:12 UTC

devon_infra: Applied model-fallback rule (acmeai) -> redirect to redwood-small for non-critical routes at 09:18:05 UTC.

ingress-bot: Config change: org-level rate-limit applied (acmeai) = 60 rps burst 20 at 09:18:07 UTC

anna_support: Customer reports immediate drop in 504s to near-zero for the last 3 minutes, thanks. They're worried about correctness with fallback though.

luis_sre: We'll need a follow-up: 1) throttle/retry guidance for customers; 2) evaluate adding jitter to client retry policy; 3) long-term: adaptive batch window + early-shed when queue_depth > 400. Filing a ticket.

devon_infra: Created internal ticket INF-4921: "Adaptive ingress shed and batch-window tuning for sustained small-request bursts". Assigned to eng-runtime.

sam_oncall: Marking incident as mitigation in place. Please add postmortem notes and customer communication. I'll stay on watch for 30m. :eyes:

anna_support: Noted, will send customer update and offer to help tune their retry backoff. Thanks all :heart:

ops-bot: DeployBot: no rolling deploys during incident window (09:10-09:40 UTC)

luis_sre: Quick note for postmortem: KV cache warmup + client retry pattern + fixed batch-window = bad combo. Repro steps saved in INF-4921.

anna_support: Closing thread once postmortem link is added.
